label: Seniors
assignment: Discover realistic resources that help older adults in {service_area} remain safe, healthy, connected, and as independent as possible. Follow aging agencies and senior centers to specific meals, transportation, benefits, caregiver, in-home, health, legal, housing, and social programs. Verify age and functional criteria, cost, waitlists, service area, assessment, and enrollment.
include: Meals, transportation, senior centers, social connection, exercise, and technology help
Benefits counseling, Medicare, Medicaid, prescription, tax, financial, and legal assistance
In-home support, personal care, homemaking, home modification, fall prevention, and caregiver respite
Adult day services, dementia support, protective services, guardianship alternatives, and long-term-care navigation
Services for isolated, rural, disabled, low-income, veteran, immigrant, and kinship-caregiving older adults
exclude: Commercial senior-living marketing without a defined assistance or affordability pathway
General adult services that do not accommodate age, mobility, cognition, or caregiving realities
Programs whose waitlists, functional criteria, or service boundaries make local access unrealistic
verificationQuestions: What age, functional need, income, caregiving, or geographic criteria apply?
Is an in-home assessment, physician certification, or benefits enrollment required?
What cost share, donation, waitlist, frequency, and transportation arrangement applies?
Can caregivers or authorized representatives initiate and coordinate service?

stages.title: Daily living and connection
stages.instruction: Investigate meals, transportation, senior centers, social connection, exercise, technology, errands, and practical supports available now, including mobility and scheduling realities.

stages.title: Benefits, health, and legal navigation
stages.instruction: Investigate Medicare, Medicaid, prescriptions, benefits, tax and financial help, legal assistance, advance planning, fraud protection, and health-navigation services.

stages.title: In-home and caregiver support
stages.instruction: Investigate personal care, homemaking, home modifications, fall prevention, respite, adult day care, dementia support, protective services, long-term-care navigation, and caregiver assessment.

stages.title: Independence and waitlist review
stages.instruction: Cross-check age and functional criteria, assessments, cost share, waitlists, rural reach, caregiver involvement, mobility, cognition, language, and transport. Identify risks where no service bridges independent living and institutional care.
